To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Pick matrix of the power spectrum of a stationary process can be identified with its state covariance, and that the power spectrum can be identified with a generalized analytic function that interpolates its state covariance.

the Pick matrix is the key to the spectral analysis problem, and that the Pick matrix can be identified with an important matrix in linear system theory, namely the state covariance matrix of a filter driven by the process.

(i) the Pick matrix of a power spectrum is the state covariance of the associated state-space representation, (ii) the Pick matrix is a Toeplitz matrix, (iii) the Pick matrix has a very special block structure, (iv) the Pick matrix and the state covariance have the same singular values, and (v) the state covariance is a non-negative definite Toeplitz matrix.
